route: Lignocellulosic: pretreatment plus enzymatic hydrolysis to glucose and xylose
sugar_equivalent_yield: 0.31 to 0.44 t SE per t air-dry straw (0.35 to 0.50 per t DM; lower value glucose only)
cost_usd_per_t_sugar: 342 to 467 (nth-plant TEAs, US); 1,320 (India, lab-optimised bagasse); straw feedstock alone 57 to 162
trl_2026: 7 to 8 (first commercial plants underperform: Panipat 62% of design in Dec 2025; Podari closed 2023)
competing_uses: Mushrooms, cattle fodder, mulch, soil return, straw rolls, biomass power (PDP8 biomass 4.8 to 7.0 GW by 2050), 2G ethanol for E15/E20
source_ids: NGF-01; NGF-02; NGF-04; NGF-05; NGF-06; NGF-07; NGF-08; NGF-10; NGF-11; NGF-34; NTS-26
notes: Paddy path 40 to 43 Mt (2030), 37 to 42 (2040), 35 to 41 (2050), our assumption from the rice-land cut (NTS-15) and the 35 Mt floor (NTS-04); straw-to-grain 1.19 (NGF-01). Mekong Delta over 24 Mt, about 30% collected and 70% burned or buried in 2025 (NGF-04). Technical SE potential 12.8 to 21.5 Mt in 2050.

stream: Rice straw, 1 million ha low-emission programme
competing_uses: Mushrooms, fodder, compost, mulch; the programme names reuse, not a use
notes: Decision 1490/QD-TTg: 100% of straw collected and reused on 1 Mha by 2030. 14 Mt would hold 4.3 to 6.2 Mt SE; the S-ALT 2050 need equals 21 to 31% of it.

sugar_equivalent_yield: 0.35 to 0.50 t SE per t DM
cost_usd_per_t_sugar: As rice straw; bagasse-specific lab TEA 1,320 (India)
competing_uses: Mill boilers and power export (QNS An Khe bagasse plant expanding to 135 MW); briquettes
notes: Cane 13.3 Mt (2025/26, FS-31) held at about 14 Mt (our assumption); bagasse 0.29 t wet per t cane at 50% moisture (NGF-09 uses 0.3). Surplus depends on mill boiler efficiency; not measured. Cane trash (tops and leaves, about 2.7 Mt at 0.2 t per t cane, NGF-09) could replace bagasse in boilers and free it.

route: Amylase hydrolysis to glucose (no cellulosic pretreatment needed); fibre fraction by 2G later
unit: Mt starch in pulp per yr
sugar_equivalent_yield: 0.97 t SE per t starch (1.08 x 90% recovery)
cost_usd_per_t_sugar: about 200 to 700 (implied pulp price VND 1,700 per kg, form unclear: dried pulp gives the low end, wet pulp the high end)
trl_2026: 6 to 7 (enzymatic pulp hydrolysis at pilot scale; yeast SCP on cassava hydrolysate in the lab)
competing_uses: Fresh pulp to cattle and pig farms; dried pulp to feed mills; biogas; fertiliser
source_ids: FS-03; FS-05; FS-06; FS-18; SCI-22; SCI-44; v0.1 app-s4 C3
notes: Starch output held at about 2.5 Mt (our assumption); pulp swings with Chinese starch demand (2024 was about 60% of 2025). Diverting pulp removes a feed carbohydrate, so the net gain is the protein made. Pulp starch = about 1.2 Mt DM x 54 to 70% starch (app-s4 C3, our calculation). Technical potential 0.63 to 0.82 Mt SE.

route: Water extraction of stem starch plus hydrolysis; fibre by 2G
sugar_equivalent_yield: 0.15 to 0.29 t SE per t DM (starch only)
competing_uses: Planting stakes (about 30% kept), fuel, left in field
notes: Stem DM 0.12 to 0.18 t per t fresh root is our harvest-index assumption; 70% not replanted (NGF-27); stem starch 14 to 42% of DM (NGF-26), 30% with 15% water-extractable (NGF-25). Dispersed upland collection is the main barrier.

sugar_equivalent_yield: 0.35 to 0.50 t SE per t DM
competing_uses: Cattle fodder and silage ('ngô sinh khối' is the only feed crop named in Decision 1748), burning, soil cover on slopes
notes: Stover 1.0 t DM per t grain (our assumption). Grain output flat to slightly falling (QNT S-BASE holds it flat). Sloping upland fields make collection costly.

sugar_equivalent_yield: 0.15 to 0.30 t SE per t (our assumption)
notes: Caffeine 0.5 to 1.3% limits feed use. Small; Dak Lak and Central Highlands.

sugar_equivalent_yield: 0.50 t SE per t (48% fermentable sugars, our assumption)
competing_uses: MSG, baker's yeast, alcohol, planned QNS An Khe molasses ethanol (about 0.37 Mt a year if built), feed
notes: First-generation by-product, already contested; Vedan reported tight molasses in H1 2026. Scales with cane.

stream: Ethanol stillage fermentables (glycerol, residual sugars, acids)
route: Direct fungal biomass on thin stillage (PEKILO-type)
volume_now: 0.22 Mt ethanol design capacity (0.02 to 0.03 Mt SE)
unit: Mt ethanol produced per yr (basis for stillage)
sugar_equivalent_yield: 0.10 to 0.15 t SE per t ethanol (our assumption)
cost_usd_per_t_sugar: near zero feedstock cost; disposal credit

notes: Ethanol path is our assumption: E10 from June 2026, E15/E20 discussed (NGF-31), about 80% of E10 ethanol imported mid-2026 (v0.1). Co-location required.

route: Direct yeast SCP on process water, or biogas then methanotroph
sugar_equivalent_yield: 0.66 t SE per t COD (70% fermentable)
cost_usd_per_t_sugar: negative to low (treatment cost avoided) but dilute (7 to 20 g COD per L)
trl_2026: 6 to 7 (direct yeast SCP on starch water, historic); 4 to 5 (methanotroph on biogas)
competing_uses: Covered-lagoon biogas for starch drying (replaces fuel oil and coal)
notes: 13 m3 per t starch and 12.2 g COD per L at a 500 t per day Thai plant (NGF-24); 2.5 Mt starch gives about 32 million m3 (v0.1 had about 22 million m3 from one Vietnamese factory ratio). As biogas: about 45 m3 CH4 per t starch, about 0.08 Mt CH4 a year nationally (our estimate); do not add to the direct route. EU feed law bans waste from wastewater treatment in feed (NGF-14).

stream: Food-industry wastewaters (tofu whey, soy milk, brewery)
notes: Our rough estimate: tofu and soy milk lose soluble sugars from about 550 kt of food soy (about 44 kt); brewery wastewater 3 to 5 L per L of beer at 2 to 4 g COD per L. Scattered; only large plants (Vinasoy, breweries) are practical.

route: Biogas or compost today; microbial protein only for non-feed uses unless rules change
sugar_equivalent_yield: 0.08 to 0.15 t SE per t wet (our assumption)
notes: 76 kg per person per year (UNEP Food Waste Index 2021 via NGF-28) x UN WPP 2024 population. EU bans household waste in feed; Vietnam only advises against untreated swill (NGF-30). Technical potential 0.6 to 1.2 Mt SE.

Faeces-derived perception and feed-law risk. National biogas figure not found (a 2024 RSER study is closed access).
